headline: Broke Dak Mountain Survives Meredith's Fan Club by Two-Tenths of a Point
meme_brief: Two teams play an entire week of fantasy football and the scoreboard ends up separated by the width of a field goal — the kind of finish that makes a guy stare at his lineup card in silence.
recap:
The closest finish of the week came down to two-tenths of a point, as Broke Dak Mountain edged Meredith's Fan Club 119.25 to 119.05. Josh Allen was the engine for the winners with 37.45 points, and the margin held up only because Meredith's Fan Club got burned by a scoreless night from DK Metcalf (0.9 points) in the starting lineup while Patrick Mahomes quietly dropped 39.65 points in the loss. It is the kind of game that will get discussed at the next gathering regardless of what anyone actually wants to talk about.

The other end of the spectrum belonged to Joe Mama Angie Daddy, who ran up 160.2 points behind a 63.1-point outburst from Joe Burrow — also the single highest individual score in the league this week — in a 72.55-point demolition of mikelanta, who got 19.45 from Caleb Williams and not much else. Chuba Bucky Doo also won comfortably, 152.45 to 125.95 over Dak to the Future, powered by a 40.65-point night from Kirk Cousins. Pukachu Chews You beat Long Live King Henry 127.9 to 116.65, and Screaming Eagles edged demon44, 125.25 to 117.0, with Drake Maye going for 31.45. Silverbacks topped Waffle House 112.9 to 93.3.

The top scorer in the league this week was Joe Burrow, and the worst bench call belonged to Chuba Bucky Doo, who started a scoreless Chris Godwin over Chris Rodriguez's 13.3 points — a mistake that didn't cost them anything in a 26.5-point win, but the second straight week that team has made exactly that kind of call. Pukachu Chews You also left points on the bench, sitting Rico Dowdle (12.6) in favor of Jordan Mason (2.0), a 10.6-point gap in a game that team still won by 11.25.
transaction_desk:
Dak to the Future spent a genuinely costly waiver priority slot (sixth of twelve) to bring back T.J. Hockenson, and the early return is fine — 14.8 points in his first week back — in a losing effort. That's a real bet that's at least shown something so far. Everything else around the league this week was priority-free: Long Live King Henry churned through two moves, briefly rostering the Washington Commanders' defense before flipping it for Jacoby Brissett, who proceeded to throw for 5.65 points in a loss — an odd piece of lineup management that cost nothing but also produced nothing.

Silverbacks ran three separate moves — Kendrick Bourne in, Devin Singletary in for Zonovan Knight, Austin Ekeler in for Tyler Higbee — none of it costing any priority since that roster sits at the back of the waiver order anyway. None of the three have scored much yet, but when the cost is zero, there's no real downside to collecting bodies. Joe Mama Angie Daddy and demon44 both made low-cost, sensible depth additions (Tyler Goodson, and Antonio Williams, who doubles as insurance behind Stefon Diggs), the kind of moves that don't make headlines but don't hurt anybody either.

Looking at results from recent weeks of adds, Michael Penix on Silverbacks keeps climbing — nearly 107 points accumulated since Week 4 for a pickup that cost nothing, which remains one of the quieter heists in the league. Aaron Rodgers has also been a free find for that same roster, sitting at 86.7 points since Week 5 with zero priority spent. Bryce Young, picked up by demon44 in Week 4 for the price of the league's worst priority slot, has been worth it too, now at 89.9 cumulative points. Meredith's Fan Club's early-season premium bid on Oronde Gadsden, by contrast, has produced only 17.2 points for a slot that was supposedly worth protecting.

standings_narrative:
With eight weeks gone, Joe Mama Angie Daddy (7-1), Chuba Bucky Doo (6-2), and Broke Dak Mountain (5-3) sit atop their divisions and would claim the three automatic playoff seeds if the season ended today. Dak to the Future (5-3) and Pukachu Chews You (4-4) currently hold the next two spots on record alone, seeds four and five. The sixth and final spot doesn't go to the next-best record — it goes to whichever remaining team has scored the most points overall, and right now that's Screaming Eagles (4-4, 969.2 points), narrowly ahead of mikelanta (3-5, 960.55 points) on the outside looking in.

That leaves Long Live King Henry, demon44, Silverbacks, Meredith's Fan Club, and Waffle House all currently outside the picture. Meredith's Fan Club in particular has the scoring profile to make a push if a few of these one-score games start breaking their way instead of against them.
look_ahead: Next week, Chuba Bucky Doo visits Joe Mama Angie Daddy in a matchup of the two best records in the league. Broke Dak Mountain hosts Screaming Eagles, a game with direct playoff-seeding implications given where the points race currently sits. Dak to the Future and mikelanta square off at the bottom of the Hearts and Diamonds mix, while Waffle House gets a shot at Pukachu Chews You. Silverbacks faces Long Live King Henry, Meredith's Fan Club takes on demon44, and the margins across the league this week suggest none of these are safe bets either way.

running_jokes: Chuba Bucky Doo has now posted a real bench mistake in back-to-back weeks and won both times anyway, carried by its quarterback spot.
Pukachu Chews You has a two-week bench mistake streak and has still won both games.
Silverbacks quietly keeps collecting free-agent value — Michael Penix and Aaron Rodgers have combined for nearly 194 points since being added for zero priority cost.
